subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw accept the additive `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle contract for sub-agent startup failures, and should it replace the stale candidate PR with a current-main implementation?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is real enough to keep open, but the fix creates a new core event surface spanning gateway, session, SDK, and subagent consumers, which needs maintainer API/product direction before automation should implement it.

options.title: Accept current-main lifecycle contract
options.body: Approve a fresh implementation of additive first-progress and startup-failed phases across current runtime and consumer surfaces, with regression tests and docs.

options.title: Narrow to failure projection only
options.body: Reject the new first-progress event for now and only fix startup aborts so they become visible terminal failures instead of timeout-shaped hangs.

options.title: Defer the event surface
options.body: Keep the issue open as product backlog until maintainers are ready to settle the lifecycle API shape.

recommendation.title: Accept current-main lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Approve a fresh implementation of additive first-progress and startup-failed phases across current runtime and consumer surfaces, with regression tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses subagent lifecycle, gateway projection, and core compatibility boundaries where steipete has relevant history and product context.
